```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Buildability within the window is directly evidenced for A. Several open-source single-developer clones (OpenPaper, Morning Paper) show the ingest-classify-render pipeline can be shipped quickly by one person with AI tools. For B, its own brief calls the core differentiator, filing the country-of-residence return, the 'hard part' that even the most advanced competitor has not solved.",
    "B has a regulatory and liability surface that A lacks. It needs IRS e-file Provider (EFIN) authorization with a suitability check and EA/attorney review, annual software acceptance testing, and GDPR counsel review. Its brief lists the EFIN timeline as an open question. That threatens a 90-day paying-customer goal, and a tax error carries real liability.",
    "A has a concrete price anchor: Edition.ink's $5/month Pro tier. A digital-only MVP avoids print capital costs. A has cited, cheap hyperlocal ad channels ($0.70–1.14 Facebook CPC, Nextdoor $2–5 CPC). B's only channel is a blended $27.66 CPL that its brief says understates the finance vertical.",
    "If B drops the local-country filing to make the window, it collapses into a US-side market with six self-serve competitors at commoditized prices. That is arguably more crowded with paid incumbents than A's niche.",
    "A's main risks are a low $5 price point, free open-source substitutes, and copyright exposure. These threaten scale and long-term viability more than they threaten landing one paying customer in 90 days. Two supporting claims in A's case against, the copyright litigation and Pew's ~9% figure, carry no source and so count as missing."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence (three Reddit quotes about PFIC/FBAR 'nightmares' and $800–$2,500 accountant quotes) speaks only to the US-side pain that six competitors already serve. Nothing in the brief shows demand or willingness to pay for the stated differentiator, combined US plus country-of-residence filing. The brief itself lists willingness to pay for a combined product as an open question.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. B has clearly stronger willingness-to-pay evidence: recent, acute pain quotes and $150–$800 price anchors against A's $5/month. A's demand quotes are old (2008–2022) letters about print newspapers being bloated, not evidence that anyone would pay for personalization. A wins mainly on feasibility and speed to a first paying customer under the 90-day, one-person constraint, not on market strength. Under a longer horizon or revenue-size criterion, B could plausibly win."
}
```
